title: Unit – 3 : Session – 5 : SLO – 1 | Declarative Programming in Databases
sections: Fill: In declarative programming, the focus is on WHAT (the result) rather than how the task is performed.
T/F: SQL is an example of a declarative programming language used in databases. — TRUE
MCQ: Best represents a declarative SQL statement → B) SELECT name FROM students WHERE grade > 90;
Fill: Declarative programming abstracts away the MECHANISM (control flow/details) of data access.
SQL Task: grade > 90 on Alice(85), Bob(92), Clara(88) → B) Bob
T/F: In declarative programming, the database engine determines the most efficient way to execute a query. — TRUE
MCQ: NOT a feature of declarative programming in databases → C) Explicit control flow
Fill: The WHERE clause in SQL is used to FILTER records in declarative queries.
Identify the error: grade => 90 → C) Invalid operator (>= is correct)
Fill: Declarative programming helps developers express logic of computation without describing its CONTROL FLOW (how it is done).
